# OfficeHQ

A full-stack office-management web application.

- **Front end:** Angular single-page app (standalone components, lazy routes), built into
  `src/main/resources/static`.
- **Back end:** Spring Boot with Spring MVC `@RestController` endpoints, on an in-memory H2 database
  with Flyway migrations run on boot.

## Build and run

```
bin/build              # build the SPA and package one runnable jar
PORT=3000 bin/start    # start the app (serves the SPA + REST on $PORT)
bin/stop               # stop it
```

Readiness: `GET /actuator/health`.

## Tests

End-to-end tests use Playwright (in `e2e/`) and bind to `data-testid`:

```
bin/e2e                # build, start, run the specs in e2e/specs, then stop
```

content.text:
Ending a recurring plan inside a period it has already billed now issues a credit note, and `bin/e2e` passes. That includes the replay of earlier tests' data.

**What happens now:** when you set an end date on a sent recurring invoice and some of its billed periods run past that date:
- A credit note dated today is created. Each line with a service period gets a credit line for the days after the end date. It's charged by the day the same way the app already prices periods (12/365 of the monthly price per day) and taxed like the original. One-off lines aren't credited.
- It's issued like any other credit note: it comes off what the invoice still owes, and anything beyond that is held as credit for the client.
- The plan has ended, so "Generate next period" is refused, as it already was for a plan past its end date.

In the test case, March 16–31 of the $450 support plan is credited at $236.71, plus 10% tax, for $260.38. That leaves $376.11 due.

**Changes:**
- `Invoice.creditsAfter(end, before)` works out the credit lines.
- `InvoiceService.setRecurUntil` builds the credit note and issues it.
- In the invoice panel, when saving the end date changes the invoice's credited amount, the client's invoice list reloads so the new credit note shows up.

**Things that behave differently from what you might assume:**
- **Moving the end date earlier a second time only credits the newly ended days.** Days after the previous end date were already credited, so they aren't credited again. To allow this, I turned off the usual "can't credit more of a line than was invoiced" check for these credit notes only. That check counts quantity, not days, so a second partial credit of the same line would otherwise be refused. The other checks on issuing a credit note still apply.
- **Drafts, void and written-off invoices just get the new end date, with no credit note.** The same goes for non-recurring invoices.
- **Only the invoice you edit is credited.** If it has already generated next month's invoice, that one isn't touched; it keeps the end date it was generated with.
